correctness.rationale: After homogeneity, phase rotation, and unitary similarity, every nonzero rank-one operator reduces to a \(2\times2\) block with singular value \(\alpha\) and overlap \(r\). The Hermitian matrix \(\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\theta}T)\) has eigenvalues \(\frac{\alpha}{2}(r\cos\theta\pm\sqrt{1-r^2\sin^2\theta})\). Taking the larger absolute value, squaring, averaging, and evaluating \(\int_0^1\sqrt{1-r^2u^2}\,du\) gives the stated closed formula. Endpoint and normalization checks agree with the focal source's sharp global bounds. The proof covers every \(r\in[0,1]\) and uses no finite-experiment surrogate.

value.rationale: Rank-one operators are a canonical test class for numerical-radius functionals, and normalized overlap is the natural complete unitary/phase invariant after scaling. The formula classifies the new radius on that entire class, identifies both sharp global comparison constants inside rank one, and provides an exact benchmark for future inequalities. This is a natural structural calculation tied directly to the newly introduced invariant rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or routine numerical increment.
